stem: A body of mass 0.2 kg performs linear S.H.M. It experiences a restoring force of 0.2 N when its displacement from the mean position is 4 cm. Determine (i) force constant (ii) period of S.H.M. and (iii) acceleration of the body when its displacement from the mean position is 1 cm.
solution:
[Textbook misprint: the book's printed working for part (iii) substitutes \( x = 0.04 \) m (4 cm, the displacement given in part (i)) instead of the 1 cm the question asks for, and so prints \( a = -1\ \text{m s}^{-2} \). The stem is preserved as printed; the working is corrected to use \( x = 0.01 \) m, giving \( a = -0.25\ \text{m s}^{-2} \).]
(i) Force constant,
\( k = f / x \)
\( = (0.2)/\,0.04 = 5 \) N/m
(ii) Period \( T = 2\pi / \omega \)
\( = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{m}{k}} = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{0.2}{5}} = 0.4\pi \) s
(iii) Acceleration
\( a = -\omega^2 x = -\frac{k}{m} x = -\frac{5}{0.2} \times 0.01 = -0.25\ \text{m s}^{-2} \)

subtopic: Acceleration, Velocity and Displacement in S.H.M.
stem: A particle performs linear S.H.M. of period 4 seconds and amplitude 4 cm. Find the time taken by it to travel a distance of 1 cm from the positive extreme position.
solution:
\( x = A \sin\left( \omega t + \phi \right) \)
Since particle performs S.H.M. from positive extreme position, \( \phi = \frac{\pi}{2} \) and from data
\( x = A - 1 = 3\,\text{cm} \)
\( \therefore 3 = 4 \sin\left( \frac{2\pi}{T} t + \frac{\pi}{2} \right) \)
\( \therefore \frac{3}{4} = \cos \frac{2\pi}{4} t = \cos \frac{\pi}{2} t \)
\( \therefore \frac{\pi}{2} t = 41.4^\circ = \left( 41.4 \times \frac{\pi}{180} \right)^{c} \)   \( \therefore t = 0.46 \) s
\( \left[ \text{Or, } \frac{180}{2} t = 41.4 \therefore t = 0.46\ \text{s} \right] \)

subtopic: Acceleration, Velocity and Displacement in S.H.M.
stem: A particle performing linear S.H.M. with period 6 second is at the positive extreme position at \( t = 0 \). The particle is found to be at a distance of 3 cm from this position at time \( t = 7 \) s, before reaching the mean position. Find the amplitude of S.H.M.
solution:
\( x = A \sin\left( \omega t + \phi \right) \)
Since particle starts \( (t = 0) \) from positive extreme position, \( \phi = \pi/2 \) and \( x = A - 3 \)
\( \therefore x = A \sin\left( \omega t + \frac{\pi}{2} \right) \)
\( \therefore A - 3 = A \sin\left( \frac{2\pi}{T} t + \frac{\pi}{2} \right) \)
\( \therefore \frac{A-3}{A} = \sin\left( \frac{2\pi}{6} \times 7 + \frac{\pi}{2} \right) \)
\( \therefore \frac{A-3}{A} = \sin\left( \frac{7\pi}{3} + \frac{\pi}{2} \right) \)
\( \therefore \frac{A-3}{A} = \sin\left( \frac{\pi}{3} + \frac{\pi}{2} \right) = \cos \frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{1}{2} \)
\( \therefore 2A - 6 = A \)
\( \therefore A = 6\,\text{cm} \)

subtopic: Acceleration, Velocity and Displacement in S.H.M.
stem: The speeds of a particle performing linear S.H.M. are 8 cm/s and 6 cm/s at respective displacements of 6 cm and 8 cm. Find its period and amplitude.
solution:
\( v = \omega \sqrt{\left( A^2 - x^2 \right)} \)
\( \therefore \frac{8}{6} = \frac{\omega \sqrt{\left( A^2 - 6^2 \right)}}{\omega \sqrt{\left( A^2 - 8^2 \right)}} \) or \( \frac{4}{3} = \frac{\omega \sqrt{\left( A^2 - 36 \right)}}{\omega \sqrt{\left( A^2 - 64 \right)}} \)
\( \therefore A = 10\,\text{cm} \)
\( v_1 = \omega \sqrt{\left( A^2 - x_1^{\,2} \right)} \)
\( \therefore 8 = \frac{2\pi}{T} \sqrt{\left( 10^2 - 6^2 \right)} \)  \( \therefore 8 = \frac{2\pi}{T} 8 \)
\( \therefore T = 6.284 \) s

subtopic: Acceleration, Velocity and Displacement in S.H.M.
stem: The maximum velocity of a particle performing S.H.M. is 6.28 cm/s. If the length of its path is 8 cm, calculate its period.
solution:
\( v_{\text{max}} = 6.28 \frac{\text{cm}}{\text{s}} = 2\pi \frac{\text{cm}}{\text{s}} \) and \( A = 4\,\text{cm} \)
\( v_{\text{max}} = A\omega = A \frac{2\pi}{T} \)
\( \therefore 2\pi = 4 \frac{2\pi}{T} \)
\( \therefore T = 4\,\text{s} \)

subtopic: Reference Circle, Phase and Graphical Representation
stem: Describe the state of oscillation if the phase angle is \( 1110^\circ \).
solution:
\( 1110^\circ = 3 \times 360^\circ + 30^\circ \)
\( 3 \times 360^\circ \) plus something indicates 4th oscillation. Now, \( A \sin 30^\circ = \frac{A}{2} \)
Thus, phase angle \( 1110^\circ \) indicates that during its 4th oscillation, the particle is at \( +A/2 \) and moving to the positive extreme.

subtopic: Reference Circle, Phase and Graphical Representation
stem: While completing its third oscillation during linear S.H.M., a particle is at \( \frac{-\sqrt{3}}{2} A \), heading to the mean position. Determine the phase angle.
solution:
\( A \sin \theta_1 = \frac{-\sqrt{3}}{2} A \)  \( \therefore \theta_1 = \left( \pi + \frac{\pi}{3} \right)^{c} \) or \( \left( 2\pi - \frac{\pi}{3} \right)^{c} \)
From negative side, the particle is heading to the mean position. Thus, the phase angle is in the fourth quadrant for that oscillation.
\( \therefore \theta_1 = \left( 2\pi - \frac{\pi}{3} \right)^{c} \)
As it is the third oscillation, phase
\( \theta = 2 \times 2\pi + \theta_1 \)  \( \therefore \theta = 4\pi + \left( 2\pi - \frac{\pi}{3} \right) \)
\( = 6\pi - \frac{\pi}{3} = \left( \frac{17\pi}{3} \right)^{c} \)
